architecture.approach: Retroactive plan of the implemented design. Projects and sprints are workspace-scoped Mongoose documents exposed by permission-guarded Express routers under /api/workspaces/:slug/projects; a task's sprint container is a Sprint ObjectId plus the project name it belongs to, kept consistent by reconcileSprint in the task controller. The backlog, sprint cards and sprint dialogs live in client/src/features/projects, while the analytical views are pure functions in feature lib folders (burndown, velocity, sprintStats, roadmap, workload, capacity) consumed by the pages under client/src/pages. Nothing in this feature adds a datastore: the sprint report is derived from the activity log the app already records.

dataModel.flowDescription: GET /api/workspaces/:slug/projects resolves the workspace from the slug, upserts a Project for every task project name that has none, then returns the projects with their sprints attached. A sprint is created inside a project, started (planned to active, startedAt) and completed (active to completed, completedAt plus completedPoints summed over the completed top-level tasks), which moves the unfinished tasks to the backlog or to a planned sprint and records those moves in Activity. A task joins a sprint by writing task.sprint together with the sprint's project name; every change is recorded in Activity, and the sprint report later replays the sprint-related changes of that log to rebuild who was committed, added, removed and completed.

securityConsiderations.description: Workspace isolation (CON-106): findProject and findSprint and every task, activity and sprint query carry workspace: req.workspace._id, so a valid ObjectId from another workspace resolves to 404 instead of returning data. Ids are cast with mongoose.isValidObjectId before use and request values are never interpolated into raw queries (CON-516).

Authorisation runs before the handler (CON-105, CON-512): projectRoutes applies protect and then requirePermission('projects:read' | 'projects:write' | 'projects:delete'), and the sprint report route requires projects:read, so a role without project access cannot read sprint scope or report data.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: listProjects fetches projects and sprints with one parallel Promise.all and groups them in memory instead of running a query per project; the roadmap, workload, burndown and velocity computations are pure functions over the already-loaded task list, memoised with useMemo in the pages.

The sprint report reads the activity log through the existing { workspace, action, createdAt } index and selects only task, changes and createdAt, then loads only the tasks that point at the sprint or appear in a recorded move.

risks.description: The sprint report depends on activity rows that expire after 365 days, so a very old sprint cannot be reconstructed exactly.
risks.mitigation: The report falls back to the tasks still pointing at the sprint and their creation dates, and the limitation is recorded as edge case EC-007.

risks.description: Completing or deleting a sprint moves tasks server-side while the client task list is a separate cache, which can show stale sprint membership.
risks.mitigation: ProjectDetailPage keys the task-dependent part of the page by a counter that increments after a sprint was completed or deleted, remounting it to fetch fresh tasks.

risks.description: A project rename has to cascade to tasks, wiki pages and custom fields or work silently leaves the project.
risks.mitigation: updateProject performs the three updates in one request with a case-insensitive collation; deleting a project instead unassigns its tasks explicitly.
